body: This is a snapshot of where each sector stands, built from Q2 FY27 results and Oct 2026 data. It is not a recommendation. Credit is in an upcycle (bank credit ~18–19% YoY, NBFC credit 15.4%), but private-bank NIMs are compressing (HDFC Bank 3.16%), PSBs lead on profit growth, and Nifty Bank traded at 1.63x P/B in Oct 2026, below its median. IT is at a growth trough (Infosys +1.5% CC YoY, guidance cut to 1–2%) with P/E ~18x against a 27x 7-year median (Jun 2026), and the debate is cyclical against structural (GenAI deflation). Pharma is the only large-cap sector above its FY26 average valuation, with the Section 232 generics review a tail risk. Specialty chemicals are past the trough in volumes but have no pricing power (CRISIL ~6% growth). Autos had a strong wholesale October (+12–16%), and the auto P/E of ~24x is near its long-term average. In capital goods, order inflows are at records (L&T ₹1.48 lakh cr) but transformer margins have peaked. In power, demand is at records (270.8 GW) and renewable additions have slowed to ~50 GW in FY27. Cement prices are recovering after a weak Q2 (UltraTech ₹974/t). Steel is in a margin upswing behind the safeguard duty. FMCG value growth is at a six-quarter high, led by rural, with the P/E below its median. QSR LFL is recovering slowly. Housing sales are flat to +3%. EMS margins are compressing after PLI. In defence, approvals are high but conversion is slow, at ~32–42x forward. Alcobev shows a premium–popular divide.

snapshot.banks: credit upcycle, NIM compression, P/B below median

title: Indian sector cycle clock as of Nov 2026
